added: packages/sandbox (@sos-2/sandbox): the bounded-execution-environment contract — filesystem scope (workspace/sandboxed-tree/none; out-of-scope access is a typed SANDBOX_FILESYSTEM_OUT_OF_SCOPE denial), network egress policy (none/allowlist over host NAMES; a call to a denied host is a typed SANDBOX_NETWORK_EGRESS_DENIED denial — no ambient network anywhere in the package), secrets isolation (injected credential values live ONLY inside the sandbox closure, resolved internally for authorized exchanges, never returned/echoed/logged/serialized — only NAMES are ever declared, mirroring the P3/P5 environment-contract discipline), and resource envelopes as injected deterministic budgets (fileWrites/fileBytes/shellCommands/networkCalls/secretReveals — the in-process realization of cpu/memory/time limits; an overrun is a typed SANDBOX_BUDGET_EXCEEDED denial). Boundary violations are TYPED DENIALS (SandboxResult OK | DENIED with a typed SandboxDenial) — never silent, never a crash; expected refusals never throw. The reference implementation (createLocalSandbox) is a deterministic, in-process, offline bounded environment whose describe() answers the merged P5 BoundedEnvironmentDescription (consumed vocabulary — filesystem scope, egress policy, isolation level, limits, environment-variable NAMES only); the in-process environment honestly grants neither host filesystem scope nor open egress (typed INVALID at construction). Disposal (end) is fail-closed: every later operation refuses with SANDBOX_ENDED and the credential closure dies with the sandbox.

packages/body-runtimes (@sos-2/body-runtimes): THREE reference bodies behind the merged P5 Harness Contract, each advertising honest capabilities. (1) CloudCodingShellBody — the disposable cloud coding/shell body, the reference implementation of the primary autonomous execution path: workspace read/write bounded by a per-task @sos-2/sandbox closure, shell exec through a deterministic in-process shell simulator with an INJECTABLE command registry (built-ins echo/cat/ls/pwd/test/exit; zero real process spawning), git operations as typed records (deterministic commit/push/PR refs and diffs), artifact capture, observation emission and a cursor-based event stream; placement cloud with NO local-device handle anywhere (its lifecycle is independent of user-device presence — pinned by tests); sandbox denials surface as truthful FAILED results carrying the typed denial code plus sandbox.denied events. (2) BrowserEvaluatorBody — capability-advertised browser journeys (open/interact) as typed records through an injectable BrowserPort (the reference ScriptedBrowserPort serves a deterministic fixture page model); the body enforces its own host allowlist on navigation; shell/git/workspace answer typed UNSUPPORTED (explicit, never silent). (3) GitHubProjectBody — repository operations (branch/commit/push/PR) as typed records through a synchronous GitHubRepositoryOperations seam carrying the P4 provider-neutral github vocabulary STRUCTURALLY (RepositoryId/BranchRef/CreateBranchInput/CommitFilesInput/CommitRef/CreatePullRequestInput/PullRequestRef/GitHubOperationOutcome/GitHubConnectionState — the P4 package is a frozen zero-dependency no-build package that built workspace packages cannot link; the web-contracts/onboarding structural precedent is followed and the field-for-field alignment with the real P4 sources is PINNED BY TEST in tests/harness-adapters via a runtime import of the P4 sources); every provider call is preceded by a sandbox-authorized typed network exchange record for api.github.com with the credential NAME (never its value); HONEST NOT_YET_CONNECTED: while the provider session is unconnected (no real credentials — validation provider accounts pending) every provider-backed write operation FAILS truthfully naming NOT_YET_CONNECTED, never fabricated; the advertisement derives its git capability from the seam's honestly-supported write subset (an unadvertised operation answers typed UNSUPPORTED before any session work) and its runtime-integration availability from the seam's connection state. All three bodies are LOCAL REFERENCE RUNTIMES — deterministic, offline-testable, satisfying the SAME Harness Contract real provider bodies will; the async P4 GitHubPort bridges onto the sync seam at the composition boundary (the frozen P5 §9 contract is synchronous by design — the async fabric/broker wrap sync bodies).

packages/harness-adapters (@sos-2/harness-adapters): the provider adapter contracts mapping the P5 Harness Contract onto the §4 integration shapes as TYPED PORTS with INJECTABLE TRANSPORTS — NativeApiTransport (the SDK-shaped typed surface, §4 tier 1, the highest control surface), McpProtocolTransport (the tool-protocol shape: listTools/callTool with JSON arguments, §4 tier 2) and LocalBridgeTransport (the companion/service-bridge command-dispatch shape, §4 tier 3); each shape has its adapter (NativeApiHarnessAdapter / McpHarnessAdapter / LocalBridgeHarnessAdapter) producing a HarnessContract over the transport, gated by the binding §3 advertisement (unsupported operations answer typed UNSUPPORTED) and reply-validated against exact typed shapes (a malformed transport reply is a truthful FAILED — never a silent success). The seam carries NO AUTHORITY: every marshaled request/reply is validated against an EXACT field set (HARNESS_REQUEST_SHAPES — a smuggled grant/permission/authority key is a typed violation naming the field, mirroring the P5 fabric anti-smuggling rule). Honest connection statuses: NOT_YET_CONNECTED for real providers (validation accounts pending; connection evidence never fabricated) with the explicit simulated marker when a reference transport backs the adapter (the P4 github-connection honesty discipline). Provider identity is provenance metadata only — selectHarnessAdapter implements the §4 rule deterministically and vendor-blind (tier availability + advertisement + connection; rank order then adapter id; pinned by provider-name-flip tests). In-process bridges (inProcessNativeApiTransport / inProcessMcpTransport / inProcessLocalBridgeTransport) serve ANY HarnessContract — including the P8 reference bodies — through every adapter shape, proving real provider endpoints attach later through the same adapters without contract change.

apps/worker-runtimes (@sos-2/worker-runtimes): the runtime host — the local reference of the external worker topology. A plain Node + TypeScript host (repo-standard ESM + tsc build, no vendor framework) that leases a reference body through the P5 broker (via the execution fabric's createBoundedTask: authority gate -> capability-based selection -> single-use lease -> contract createTask -> durable §6 record), executes a bounded task's step program through the fabric's uniform gate pipeline (TASK -> LEASE -> AUTHORITY -> ADVERTISEMENT -> DISPATCH — observations and artifacts land in the typed boundaries automatically), and releases the body through Spirit-side completion (§10): the verification record is built from the executed step outcomes (evidence refs = observation ids + captured artifact ids); a denied, unsupported or failed step stops the program and completes the task with verified:false — honest, never fabricated. NO long-running work inside any request lifetime: the host runs on an INJECTED tick/command source (WorkerCommand union + CommandSource port + UserDevicePresence port; poll-driven ticks, a bounded drain, no ambient timers — testable offline). The §7 user-device model is enforced at the scheduling gate: cloud/remote bodies run regardless of device presence (the task continues while the user's computer is off — pinned by tests with the device reported offline and zero device probes), user-device work orders QUEUE while the device is offline and run when it returns. Body replacement rides fabric.replaceBodyForTask through the host command surface. The composition root (system-clock.ts + index.ts, the apps/api precedent) is the single impure boundary; createReferenceWorkerRuntime assembles the durable in-memory P2 stores + broker + fabric + host with everything injected.

tests/harness-adapters (@sos-2/harness-adapter-contracts): the acceptance suites. All three bodies execute COMPLETE bounded tasks through the PUBLIC §9 contract behind the P5 broker (lease -> execute -> release, lease RELEASED terminal after completion, task state surviving the body); the cloud journey runs identically through every adapter shape (native-api / mcp-protocol / local-bridge) and with the user's computer offline (zero device probes); sandbox boundary violations (filesystem out-of-scope escape, fileWrites/shellCommands budget overruns) surface as typed denials inside truthful FAILED results with durable violation observations; secrets never echo (output scans over every harness result, durable observation event, artifact record, advertisement, identity, environment description and network exchange across the full journeys); the GitHub-aware body executes the connected repository journey as typed records (provider branch head moves to the deterministic commit sha) and fails honestly with NOT_YET_CONNECTED while unconnected; the P4 vocabulary alignment is pinned field-for-field against the real P4 github package sources (statuses/scopes deep-equal, slug behavior identical, BranchRef/CommitRef/PullRequestRef/GitHubConnectionState field sets exact); adapter replacement preserves task semantics (a native-api-served body replaced mid-task by an mcp-protocol-served body under the P5 broker's replaceBodyLease — same task id, checkpoint and observations preserved, ended lease REVOKED terminal, new lease live, replacement fails closed with NO_BODY_AVAILABLE when no equivalent body exists); and structural scans: zero new external dependencies (workspace:* + the existing toolchain only, checked against the base lockfile), offline determinism (no Date.now/Math.random/fetch/process.env/timers/child_process in the owned sources outside the documented apps/worker-runtimes composition boundary), the repository's fixed vitest seed, no imports of the P3 package (structural isolation), and only merged + P8-owned workspace imports (unmerged siblings are never dependencies).
